# RFC 0001 hyphence test vectors.
#
# Each non-comment line: name\tinput-b64\toutcome\texpected-b64
#
# Outcomes are namespaced by the owning harness so multiple test
# harnesses can share this single canonical vector file. An unknown
# outcome inside a harness's own namespace is a typo and fatals;
# outcomes in another harness's namespace are skipped.
#
# Outcomes:
#   legacy/parse-ok                            - DecodeFrom must succeed; blob bytes
#                                                (captured via BlobTeeWriter) must
#                                                equal the base64-decoded expected
#                                                field.
#   legacy/parse-error-missing-separator       - DecodeFrom must error with
#                                                errors.Is(err, errMissingNewline-
#                                                AfterBoundary).
#   document/parse-error-invalid-prefix        - MetadataValidator (via Reader) must
#                                                error with errors.Is(err,
#                                                ErrInvalidPrefix).
#   document/parse-error-malformed-line        - MetadataValidator (via Reader) must
#                                                error with errors.Is(err,
#                                                ErrMalformedMetadataLine).
#   document/parse-error-unterminated-metadata - Reader must error with errors.Is(err,
#                                                ErrUnterminatedMetadata): input ends
#                                                inside the metadata section (Rust:
#                                                Error::UnterminatedMetadata).
#   document/parse-error-inline-body-with-at   - Reader must succeed; the post-
#                                                ReadFrom validator state must show
#                                                an @-line was seen AND a body section
#                                                followed (the validate subcommand
#                                                surfaces ErrInlineBodyWithAtReference
#                                                from this state).
#   grammar/reject                             - the content-grammar harness
#                                                (grammar_vectors_test.go) must find
#                                                that the document's content-grammar-
#                                                governed metadata lines do NOT parse
#                                                under docs/rfcs/hyphence-content.peg
#                                                via any real content production.
#                                                Envelope decode must still SUCCEED:
#                                                these pin content-grammar negatives,
#                                                not malformed documents, so the
#                                                envelope harnesses skip them by the
#                                                namespace rule above.
#   head/canonical                             - the typed-head harnesses (Go
#                                                head_vectors_test.go, Rust
#                                                conformance.rs) must decode the
#                                                input into a typed head, encode it
#                                                with the RFC 0005 canonical encoder,
#                                                and get exactly the base64-decoded
#                                                expected field; encoding the
#                                                expected bytes again must reproduce
#                                                them (idempotence). Input and
#                                                expected are both content-grammar
#                                                valid, so the grammar harnesses check
#                                                every line of the input too.
#
# Comment lines start with #. Blank lines are ignored.
#
# Plain-text view of each input:
#   minimal-no-body          : "---\n! toml-type-v1\n---\n"
#   body-with-separator      : "---\n! md\n---\n\nhello\n" -> blob "hello\n"
#   body-without-separator   : "---\n! toml-type-v1\n---\nfile-extension = 'png'\n"
#                              (no blank line after closing ---; strict default rejects)

minimal-no-body	LS0tCiEgdG9tbC10eXBlLXYxCi0tLQo=	legacy/parse-ok	
body-with-separator	LS0tCiEgbWQKLS0tCgpoZWxsbwo=	legacy/parse-ok	aGVsbG8K
body-without-separator	LS0tCiEgdG9tbC10eXBlLXYxCi0tLQpmaWxlLWV4dGVuc2lvbiA9ICdwbmcnCg==	legacy/parse-error-missing-separator	-

malformed-no-space	LS0tCiFub3NwYWNlCi0tLQoK	document/parse-error-malformed-line	-
inline-body-with-at-ref	LS0tCkAgYmxha2UyYjI1Ni1hYmMKISBtZAotLS0KCmlubGluZQo=	document/parse-error-inline-body-with-at	-

# New vectors for RFC 0002 (content grammar). Content is still opaque at
# these envelope-level harnesses (RFC 0001 §Conformance) — none of these
# vectors exercise RFC 0002's content-grammar productions themselves, only
# that documents using RFC 0002's new content spellings remain RFC
# 0001-envelope-conforming, per RFC 0002's "existing decoders remain
# conforming" scope boundary. legacy/parse-ok's decoder
# (TypedMetadataCoderDefault) only wires `!` and `@`, so the unified-lock
# form on a `!` line is the only one that fits that outcome; the `-`/`<`
# forms need the full six-prefix decoder (document/parse-ok, added
# alongside these vectors).
#
# Plain-text view:
#   unified-lock-type              : "---\n! md @blake2b256-abc\n---\n"
#   unified-lock-reference         : "---\n! md\n- one/uno @blake2b256-def\n---\n"
#   field-predicate-line           : "---\n! task\n- due=\"2026-08-01\"\n---\n"
#   deprecated-angle-still-accepted: "---\n! task\n< blocks=other/task @blake2b256-ghi\n---\n"
#   id-less-field-lock             : "---\n! organize\n- _base=@blake2b256-jkl\n---\n"

unified-lock-reference	LS0tCiEgbWQKLSBvbmUvdW5vIEBibGFrZTJiMjU2LWRlZgotLS0K	document/parse-ok	-
field-predicate-line	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotIGR1ZT0iMjAyNi0wOC0wMSIKLS0tCg==	document/parse-ok	-
deprecated-angle-still-accepted	LS0tCiEgdGFzawo8IGJsb2Nrcz1vdGhlci90YXNrIEBibGFrZTJiMjU2LWdoaQotLS0K	document/parse-ok	-
id-less-field-lock	LS0tCiEgb3JnYW5pemUKLSBfYmFzZT1AYmxha2UyYjI1Ni1qa2wKLS0tCg==	document/parse-ok	-

# RFC 0002 revised 2026-07-18: trailing line comments (`!`/`@`/`-`/`<`
# only, never `#` free text). This vector demonstrates the
# quoting-composes case the revision calls out explicitly: the `%`
# inside the quoted field value is content, not a comment boundary.
# Plain-text view:
#   trailing-comment-quoting-composes : "---\n! task\n- note=\"50% done\" % real comment\n---\n"

trailing-comment-quoting-composes	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotIG5vdGU9IjUwJSBkb25lIiAlIHJlYWwgY29tbWVudAotLS0K	document/parse-ok	-

# RFC 0002 revised 2026-07-20: the required space before a trailing
# comment's `%` is dropped (SP made optional, not required) — `%` is
# already self-delimiting (Reserved rune, excluded from every token
# charset), so a glued comment parses identically to a spaced one.
# Plain-text view:
#   trailing-comment-glued : "---\n! md%glued comment\n---\n"

trailing-comment-glued	LS0tCiEgbWQlZ2x1ZWQgY29tbWVudAotLS0K	legacy/parse-ok	-

# RFC 0003 (supersedes RFC 0002 §Lock grammar, 2026-07-18): a locked
# value is one atomic purpose-full markl id (no space before `@`),
# not a `SP @digest` suffix. unified-lock-type/unified-lock-reference/
# deprecated-angle-still-accepted above still decode fine (content is
# opaque at this envelope layer either way) but no longer demonstrate
# the canonical spelling — see RFC 0003 §Test Vectors.
#
# Digest payloads here are BLECH32-VALID (hyphence#11). The grammar's
# digest slot is charset-strict — `Digest <- Format '-' DataChar+
# !IdentRune`, over piggy's imported DataChar — and the blech32 alphabet
# omits `b`, `i`, `o`, and `1` (piggy RFC 0011 §3.1). The former `-abc`
# and `-ghi` placeholders predate that strictness and would now be
# rejected on their `b`/`i`; they read `-acd` and `-ghj` instead. These
# are still arbitrary placeholders, not real digests — only their
# CHARSET matters, since the grammar is deliberately length-agnostic and
# checksum validity is a decoder concern.
# Plain-text view:
#   atomic-lock-type               : "---\n! md@blake2b256-acd\n---\n"
#   atomic-lock-reference           : "---\n! md\n- one/uno@blake2b256-def\n---\n"
#   atomic-lock-typed-edge           : "---\n! task\n- blocks=task/other@blake2b256-ghj\n---\n"
#   atomic-key-material-papi-shape  : "---\n! task\n- piggy-piv_auth-v1@ssh_ecdsa_nistp256_pub-qqxyz\n---\n"

atomic-lock-type	LS0tCiEgbWRAYmxha2UyYjI1Ni1hY2QKLS0tCg==	legacy/parse-ok	-
atomic-lock-reference	LS0tCiEgbWQKLSBvbmUvdW5vQGJsYWtlMmIyNTYtZGVmCi0tLQo=	document/parse-ok	-
atomic-lock-typed-edge	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotIGJsb2Nrcz10YXNrL290aGVyQGJsYWtlMmIyNTYtZ2hqCi0tLQo=	document/parse-ok	-
atomic-key-material-papi-shape	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotIHBpZ2d5LXBpdl9hdXRoLXYxQHNzaF9lY2RzYV9uaXN0cDI1Nl9wdWItcXF4eXoKLS0tCg==	document/parse-ok	-

# RFC 0003 revision (2026-07-18): MarklTerm's quoted-purpose form and
# the canonical spaced `=` field emission this revision standardizes.
# Plain-text view:
#   quoted-purpose-marklterm : "---\n! task\n- \"my thing\"@blake2b256-xyz\n---\n"
#   spaced-field-emission    : "---\n! task\n- due = \"2026-08-01\"\n---\n"

quoted-purpose-marklterm	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotICJteSB0aGluZyJAYmxha2UyYjI1Ni14eXoKLS0tCg==	document/parse-ok	-
spaced-field-emission	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotIGR1ZSA9ICIyMDI2LTA4LTAxIgotLS0K	document/parse-ok	-

# hyphence#11: the charset-strict digest slot, and the quoted-purpose
# join rune.
#
# marklterm-quoted-purpose-with-join-rune pins the case where a quoted
# purpose CONTAINS `@`: quoting is the escape mechanism, so it must be
# able to carry the very rune it escapes. The join is then the SECOND
# `@`, which means a decoder MUST locate it with a quote-aware scan and
# never with the first one. piggy treats this as its single most
# divergence-prone point (RFC 0011 §2.2, piggy#227) and trellis pins it
# too; hyphence previously pinned only the space-carrying
# `"my thing"@...` form, leaving this shape unguarded.
#
# digest-junk-non-blech32 pins the property the imported DataChar buys
# over the former permissive `'@' Ident` digest slot: `blake2b256-9bt3`
# MUST be rejected, because `b` is outside the blech32 alphabet and is
# therefore an IdentRune sitting immediately after the `9` DataChar run
# — which the `!IdentRune` anchor refuses instead of silently accepting
# a truncated `9`. Under the old permissive slot this parsed happily, so
# without this vector the tightening could regress unnoticed. The
# document is ENVELOPE-valid; only its content is ill-formed, hence
# grammar/reject rather than a document/parse-error-* outcome.
# Plain-text view:
#   marklterm-quoted-purpose-with-join-rune : "---\n! task\n- \"a@b\"@blake2b256-xyz\n---\n"
#   digest-junk-non-blech32                 : "---\n! md@blake2b256-9bt3\n---\n"

marklterm-quoted-purpose-with-join-rune	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotICJhQGIiQGJsYWtlMmIyNTYteHl6Ci0tLQo=	document/parse-ok	-
digest-junk-non-blech32	LS0tCiEgbWRAYmxha2UyYjI1Ni05YnQzCi0tLQo=	grammar/reject	-

# hyphence RFC 0002 revision (2026-08-30): '(' and ')' become Reserved
# runes so a parenthetical is self-delimiting, the precondition for
# trellis (cutting-garden RFC 0014) to define `(…)` as a META QUALIFIER
# term (cutting-garden native-tags G10). bare-paren-in-ident pins the
# consequence: a bare identifier containing '(' no longer parses as one
# Ident (DashContent's FieldContent alternative fails for want of '=',
# and RefContent's Ident+EOF fails on the unconsumed "(1)"). The quoted
# twin shows the escape hatch: the same payload inside a quoted field
# value still parses, since String consumes '(' as ordinary content.
# Plain-text view:
#   bare-paren-in-ident    : "---\n! task\n- tag(1)\n---\n"
#   quoted-paren-in-value  : "---\n! task\n- tag=\"c(1)\"\n---\n"

bare-paren-in-ident	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotIHRhZygxKQotLS0K	grammar/reject	-
quoted-paren-in-value	LS0tCiEgdGFzawotIHRhZz0iYygxKSIKLS0tCg==	document/parse-ok	-

# RFC 0005 (typed head, canonical emission). Each vector is input ->
# canonical bytes under the head/canonical outcome. Canonical form: prefix
# order `#`, `-`, `@`, `!` with `-` lines in input order; `<` written
# `-`; field lines spaced; a text bare when it is an Ident, else
# double-quoted with the Doddish escapes; a markl purpose bare when it
# fits marklid's PurposeBare, else quoted; comments kept, a trailing
# comment written ` %text`. Literal backslashes below are part of the
# document text.
# Plain-text view (input => expected):
#   head-canonical-value-kinds
#     "---\n! task\n- bare=open\n- quoted=\"two words\"\n- markl=piggy-piv_auth-v1@ssh_ecdsa_nistp256_pub-qqxyz\n- idless=@blake2b256-jkl\n- requoted=\"open\"\n---\n"
#     => "---\n- bare = open\n- quoted = \"two words\"\n- markl = piggy-piv_auth-v1@ssh_ecdsa_nistp256_pub-qqxyz\n- idless = @blake2b256-jkl\n- requoted = open\n! task\n---\n"
#   head-canonical-quoted-field-name
#     "---\n! task\n- \"odd name\"=\"v\"\n- \"plain\"=v\n---\n"
#     => "---\n- \"odd name\" = v\n- plain = v\n! task\n---\n"
#   head-canonical-locked-type-and-reference
#     "---\n! md@blake2b256-acd\n- one/uno@blake2b256-def\n- tag\n---\n"
#     => "---\n- one/uno@blake2b256-def\n- tag\n! md@blake2b256-acd\n---\n"
#   head-canonical-purpose-spelling (quoted purpose holding the join rune;
#   quoted purpose that can be bare; Ident purpose outside PurposeBare)
#     "---\n! task\n- \"a@b\"@blake2b256-xyz\n- k=\"md\"@blake2b256-acd\n- j=caldav:x@blake2b256-acd\n---\n"
#     => "---\n- \"a@b\"@blake2b256-xyz\n- k = md@blake2b256-acd\n- j = \"caldav:x\"@blake2b256-acd\n! task\n---\n"
#   head-canonical-unspaced-to-spaced (and `<` re-emitted as `-`)
#     "---\n! task\n- due=\"2026-08-01\"\n< blocks=other/task@blake2b256-ghj\n---\n"
#     => "---\n- due = 2026-08-01\n- blocks = other/task@blake2b256-ghj\n! task\n---\n"
#   head-canonical-comments-kept
#     "---\n! md%type note\n% lead\n- k=v%glued\n# d\n% tail\n---\n"
#     => "---\n# d\n% lead\n- k = v %glued\n! md %type note\n% tail\n---\n"
#   head-canonical-escapes (a LF in a value stays the two characters \n)
#     "---\n! task\n- note=\"a\\\"b\\\\c\\td\"\n- nl=\"a\\nb\"\n- odd=\"x\\qy z\"\n---\n"
#     => "---\n- note = \"a\\\"b\\\\c\\td\"\n- nl = \"a\\nb\"\n- odd = \"xqy z\"\n! task\n---\n"
#   head-canonical-body
#     "---\n! md\n# d\n---\n\nbody\n" => "---\n# d\n! md\n---\n\nbody\n"

# An empty body is not no body: the blank separator with nothing after it
# is a body section of zero bytes (Rust Some(empty), Go hasBody), so the
# canonical encoder keeps the separator. And EOF inside the metadata
# section is an error (RFC 0001 §Conformance), not a truncated head.
# Plain-text view:
#   head-canonical-empty-body       : "---\n! md\n---\n\n" => "---\n! md\n---\n\n"
#   unterminated-metadata           : "---\n! md\n- k=v\n"

# Consumer-shape exemplars: the record kinds circus EPIC 0001 D1 proposes
# to carry as hyphence (hyphence#17; circus
# docs/plans/2026-10-22-d1-capability-artifact-and-grant-chain.md, sections
# 2, 2a, 6). Values are illustrative placeholders, not real grants, keys
# or digests; what these pin is that the line shapes parse under the
# content grammar and have one canonical spelling. They say nothing about
# whether a chain verifies — that is circus/spinclass's suite. Names give
# the D1 vector each shape comes from. Note the run-root vector: a right
# that is a locked grammar reference has a markl purpose with `:`, which
# is outside PurposeBare, so its canonical spelling quotes the purpose.
